key_insight: WildClawBench exposes how real-world, long-horizon agent behavior differs from sandbox tests by providing a native-runtime, bilingual, multimodal benchmark of 60 human-authored tasks — showing agents must be evaluated in the environments where they run, not just mock sandboxes.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between synthetic, short-horizon benchmark environments and real deployment runtimes by measuring agent performance on realistic, multi-step tasks executed via native CLI harnesses and real services.
method: Curate 60 human-authored tasks that are bilingual and multimodal, designed to require long-horizon, stepwise actions.
Run agents in native runtime using a CLI harness and real service interactions (no mocked APIs) to evaluate actual end-to-end behavior and failure modes.
Use step-level/state-aware evaluation (not just final-answer checks) to measure task completion, robustness, and recovery over long sequences.
impact: Provides practitioners a more faithful benchmark to diagnose real deployment weaknesses, prioritize hardening (robustness, error recovery, grounding), and compare agent designs under realistic runtime constraints — improving readiness for production use.
visual_elements: System diagram: user → LLM/VLM agent → CLI harness → real services, highlighting native-runtime loop
Timeline / flowchart of a long-horizon task showing multiple dependent steps and intermediate checks
Bar/line chart comparing success rates and error modes on traditional sandbox benchmarks vs WildClawBench
Example bilingual multimodal task card (image + text) with expected stepwise actions and pass/fail annotations
paper_title: WildClawBench: A Benchmark for Real-World, Long-Horizon Agent Evaluation
paper_authors: Shuangrui Ding, Xuanlang Dai, Long Xing, Shengyuan Ding, Ziyu Liu
